summary: Brings together course-level graduate futures claims from 2.1.1 with wider institutional evidence to create a coherent account of the King’s graduate premium and a family of compelling, audience-specific evidence packs.
detailSummary:
This deliverable provides the institutional continuation of the course-level work in 2.1.1. It brings together the claims and evidence developed with course teams alongside graduate outcomes, skills and experiential learning evidence, wider student opportunities, alumni and employer insight and other sources of value across King’s.

The aim is to understand what these distributed sources of graduate value add up to collectively, while retaining the distinctive contribution of individual courses and disciplines. This creates a maintained institutional account of the King’s graduate premium, showing what a King’s education enables students to know, do and contribute, where that value is particularly distinctive and where it could be strengthened further.

The evidence is then translated into a family of high-quality graduate premium packs for different audiences and purposes. These may include international and domestic recruitment, faculty and disciplinary positioning, employer and partner engagement and wider institutional communication. Packs combine robust data with case studies, student and alumni voices, rich video narratives and other evidence to communicate the value of a King’s education in ways that are credible, distinctive and persuasive.
problemSolved: King’s creates substantial graduate value across its courses and wider student experience, but does not yet have a coherent institutional mechanism for bringing that distributed evidence together into a persuasive account of the graduate premium.
whatChanges: Course-owned graduate futures claims from 2.1.1 are combined with wider institutional evidence to create a maintained account of the King’s graduate premium and a family of audience-specific evidence packs.

caseForChange.problem:
King’s creates graduate value at multiple levels. Individual courses develop distinctive disciplinary knowledge, capabilities and routes into graduate futures, while the wider King’s experience adds further value through skills development, experiential learning, co-curricular opportunity, employer and alumni connection, purpose, networks and other forms of enhancement.

Through 2.1.1, course teams will have a consistent way to bring together graduate futures evidence, interpret it responsibly and develop credible course-owned claims about the value their programmes create. What King’s does not yet have is the corresponding institutional mechanism for bringing those claims together with the wider sources of graduate value across the university.

Without that second layer, strong course-level evidence remains distributed. The collective contribution of curriculum and wider graduate-futures activity is difficult to see in the aggregate, and external-facing teams can be left relying on broad institutional claims, isolated statistics or individual stories rather than a rich and coherent body of evidence about the value of a King’s education.
caseForChange.opportunity:
2.4.1 provides the institutional continuation of the course-level work in 2.1.1.

Course-owned graduate futures claims, evidence and narratives can be brought together with institutional outcomes data, skills and experiential learning evidence, wider student opportunities, alumni and employer insight and other relevant sources to build a maintained account of the King’s graduate premium.

This creates a way to understand what the diverse value created across King’s adds up to collectively, while retaining the distinctive contribution of individual courses and disciplines.

The evidence can then be translated into a family of compelling, audience-specific graduate premium packs. These can combine robust data, case studies, student and alumni voices, rich video narratives and other evidence, configured for purposes such as international and domestic recruitment, faculty and disciplinary positioning, employer and partner engagement and wider institutional communication.

Together, 2.1.1 and 2.4.1 therefore operate as bookends: one enables courses to understand and claim their graduate futures value; the other activates those claims, alongside wider institutional activity, into a coherent and persuasive account of the King’s graduate premium.
caseForChange.whyNow:
Graduate outcomes, employability and the wider value of university education are becoming increasingly important to student choice, institutional reputation, regulatory narratives and public debate. At a time of pressure on the graduate premium and intensifying competition for students, King’s needs to do more than make general claims about the advantages of its education. It needs to demonstrate them persuasively.

At the same time, King’s is creating the conditions to do this with substantially greater confidence. 2.1.1 will establish a consistent course-level evidence and sense-making model, while connected work on skills, experiential learning, student purpose, wider opportunities and graduate outcomes intelligence is making more of the value created across the institution visible and evidenceable.

There is therefore an opportunity to connect these strands as they mature, rather than allow them to remain separate initiatives. Doing so gives King’s a stronger institutional proposition and equips faculties, recruitment teams and other external-facing colleagues with richer and more credible evidence of what a King’s education enables.
caseForChange.intendedChange:
King’s moves from a collection of course-level and institutional graduate-futures evidence to a connected model in which those sources reinforce one another.

The claims and evidence developed with course teams through 2.1.1 flow into a maintained institutional account of the graduate premium, alongside evidence of the wider skills, experiences, relationships and opportunities that enrich a King’s education. King’s can see the collective story those sources tell, where its graduate premium is particularly distinctive and where further strengthening would add value.

That evidence is made usable through a family of high-quality graduate premium packs, combining data and rich narrative evidence for different faculties, disciplines, markets and external audiences. King’s is consequently better able to assert, evidence and communicate the value its students take into the world.
